Its front reaches the upper edge of the west zebra at about 132.3 (proxy about 210-215, 380 in C3902 coordinates). It crosses the top (slip-lane) section of the zebra at steady speed, and its rear clears the lower-left edge at about 134.2 (a small asphalt gap is already visible at 134.2 and 134.3). The problem is where the pedestrians were. Throughout 132.3-134.3 no pedestrian is on the slip-lane section of the zebra or at the corner stepping onto it. That section is empty except for the car in every 0.2 s frame (out/sheets/fty_c3902_1323/car_02.jpg, west_05.jpg). The group of about 8 is on the next section, past the island line. That line runs from the centre triangle's lower-left corner (proxy about 229,404) to the bottom-left triangle (apex about 146,446, right vertex about 187,484). The nearest pedestrian is the woman in the black abaya, whose feet were at about proxy (270,505) at 133.0-133.4. That is about 100-110 proxy px on the far side of the island line and roughly 105 proxy px from the car's nearest point, about 4-6 m on this part of the image (walking pace gives about 26 px/m horizontally, less vertically). The rest of the group (the white-shirt leaders at about 310-340, 420-470) is farther away. They were walking NW towards the slip lane and reached its section only around 136.0-136.5, about 2 s after the car had left. They kept a steady pace, and nobody slowed, stopped or changed direction. So the car never passed in front of a pedestrian on its own section of the crossing, and nobody on the zebra had to change speed because of it. The pedestrians were beyond the channelising island line, several metres away, and not next to the car's path. The labeller also marked it borderline. It is not a better fit for any other class: there was no braking or swerve, so it is not a near_miss, and the turn was from the kerb-side slip lane, which is correct. Since I am unsure it meets the definition, I reject it.
